**Thinking as this farmer:**

I've been working these fields my whole life. My husband goes to the city for work sometimes, so I manage most of this myself with help from my son during busy season. We have about 9 mu of land total. Around here — everyone grows winter wheat and summer corn on the same fields. I rotate them every year, same as my parents did. That's just how you farm in Quzhou.

For wheat, I always plant in October. I buy improved seed from the village supply station — they stopped selling the old kinds anyway, and the improved ones do better. I put down compound fertilizer before planting and urea at jointing. I irrigate — the well is our lifeline. Usually 3-4 times for wheat: once in winter to protect the roots from freezing, once at jointing, once heading. Maybe one more if it's dry at grain fill. My neighbor uses less water now but I'm not willing to risk the yield.

After wheat harvest in June, I plant corn on the same land right away. I use hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 or whatever the station recommends that year. Corn doesn't need as much water, the summer rains help. I fertilize at planting and again when the corn is knee-high.

I keep about 1 mu near the house for vegetables — garlic, cabbage, scallions — for the family and to sell a little at the market.
